section: Domain G — Accounting and financial reporting
citation: IFRS 9
requirement: Classify financial assets at initial recognition into amortised cost, fair value through other comprehensive income (FVOCI), or fair value through profit or loss (FVTPL) under IFRS 9, determined by the business model for managing the asset and whether its cash flows are solely payments of principal and interest (the SPPI test). Classify financial liabilities at amortised cost or FVTPL accordingly, and document the business-model and SPPI assessment supporting each classification.
fulfilmentPolicy: Accounting Policies (IFRS)

section: Domain G — Accounting and financial reporting
citation: IFRS 9
requirement: Recognise expected credit losses on financial assets measured at amortised cost and FVOCI, and on loan commitments and financial guarantees, under the IFRS 9 three-stage impairment model — 12-month ECL at Stage 1, lifetime ECL on a significant increase in credit risk at Stage 2, and lifetime ECL with interest on the net carrying amount once credit-impaired at Stage 3. Estimate ECL on a probability-weighted, forward-looking basis incorporating macroeconomic scenarios.
fulfilmentPolicy: IFRS 9 Expected Credit Loss (ECL) Provisioning Policy

section: Domain G — Accounting and financial reporting
citation: IFRS 9 (CEO election F1)
requirement: Apply IFRS 9 hedge accounting (the IAS 39 carryover option is not elected per CEO election F1), designating and documenting qualifying hedging relationships — fair-value, cash-flow or net-investment hedges — and demonstrating an economic relationship, that credit risk does not dominate, and an appropriate hedge ratio. Measure and record hedge effectiveness and any ineffectiveness each reporting period.
fulfilmentPolicy: Hedge Accounting Policy

section: Domain G — Accounting and financial reporting
citation: IFRS 7
requirement: Disclose the nature and extent of risks arising from financial instruments under IFRS 7 — credit risk, liquidity risk and market risk — together with the bank's objectives, policies and processes for managing those risks, on both a qualitative and quantitative basis. Provide the prescribed sensitivity, maturity and credit-quality analyses in the annual financial statements.
fulfilmentPolicy: Accounting Policies (IFRS); Financial Reporting & Disclosure Policy

section: Domain G — Accounting and financial reporting
citation: IFRS 13
requirement: Measure fair value under IFRS 13 as the price to sell an asset or transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date, maximising observable inputs and minimising unobservable ones. Classify each measurement within the fair-value hierarchy (Level 1 quoted prices, Level 2 observable inputs, Level 3 unobservable inputs) and provide the prescribed valuation-technique and hierarchy disclosures.
fulfilmentPolicy: Accounting Policies (IFRS)

section: Domain G — Accounting and financial reporting
citation: IFRS 15
requirement: Recognise revenue from contracts with customers under the IFRS 15 five-step model — identify the contract, identify the performance obligations, determine the transaction price, allocate it to the performance obligations, and recognise revenue as each obligation is satisfied. Apply this to fee- and commission-based banking income (interest income falls under IFRS 9 effective-interest, outside IFRS 15).
fulfilmentPolicy: Accounting Policies (IFRS)

section: Domain G — Accounting and financial reporting

requirement: Recognise leases on the balance sheet under IFRS 16 by bringing a right-of-use asset and a corresponding lease liability into account for lessee contracts (subject to the short-term and low-value exemptions), and depreciate the asset while unwinding interest on the liability. Apply lessor accounting (finance or operating lease classification) where the bank is a lessor.
fulfilmentPolicy: Accounting Policies (IFRS)

fulfilmentPolicy: Accounting Policies (IFRS)

section: Domain G — Accounting and financial reporting

section: Domain M-MK-RPT — Margin Regulatory Reporting (JN 2/2024)
requirement: Submit regulatory reporting returns containing the margin metrics set out in Appendix A of JN 2/2024 to the Authorities (FSCA and PA jointly) for every non-centrally cleared OTC derivative transaction entered into with a counterparty or foreign counterparty; the reporting obligation applies regardless of whether the JS 2/2020 margin thresholds or minimum transfer amounts are met.
fulfilmentPolicy: Trade Reporting Policy (Umoja sub-pipeline); Margin Policy

section: Domain M-MK-RPT — Margin Regulatory Reporting (JN 2/2024)
requirement: Submit the completed regulatory return to the PA via the Umoja portal using one of three approved transmission methods — Excel upload using the Umoja portal template, in-portal submission, or machine-to-machine submission via the Umoja portal API (specifications available on the Umoja portal); submit on a daily T+1 basis by no later than 16:00 South African time; on public holidays, submit on the first business day immediately following the public holiday.
fulfilmentPolicy: Trade Reporting Policy (Umoja sub-pipeline); IT/API Connectivity Procedure

section: Domain M-MK-RPT — Margin Regulatory Reporting (JN 2/2024)
citation: JN 2/2024 Appendix A (MR Version 1 Schema)
requirement: Populate and transmit the regulatory reporting metrics as defined in the MR Version 1 Schema definitions and formsets (SARB website schema specification) covering: initial margin posted/received; variation margin posted/received; counterparty identification (LEI); netting-set information; and other margin-related data elements required under JS 2/2020 §6A. The schema is available as a ZIP file at the SARB website and the Umoja portal; machine-to-machine submissions must use the Umoja portal API specifications.
fulfilmentPolicy: Trade Reporting Policy; Margin Policy; Anya schema-registry

section: Domain M-ODP-AUTH — ODP Authorisation Criteria (CS 1/2018)
requirement: Maintain capital, retained earnings and reserves proportional to ODP business risks; hold sufficient equity-funded liquid net assets to cover at least six months of operating expenses and to ensure an orderly wind-up of at least six months under stress scenarios; safeguard assets at supervised regulated entities; maintain a controlling-body-approved plan for raising additional equity if capital falls below the required level; and furnish the FSCA with a quarterly report detailing the liquid-net-asset calculation.
fulfilmentPolicy: Capital Management Policy; ICAAP; ODP Authorisation Policy

section: Domain M-ODP-AUTH — ODP Authorisation Criteria (CS 1/2018)
requirement: Ensure every member of the controlling body and every senior manager is honest and has integrity; disclose proactively all relevant facts to the FSCA; submit completed Annexure B and C Forms in respect of each controlling-body member and senior manager; and continuously satisfy the FSCA that none of the disqualifying factors in §4.2.1(3)(a)–(f) apply (criminal/civil findings of dishonesty, professional-body sanctions, regulatory-body sanctions, licence suspension/withdrawal, court-ordered disqualification from company management).
fulfilmentPolicy: Fit-and-Proper Policy; Governance Framework

section: Domain M-ODP-AUTH — ODP Authorisation Criteria (CS 1/2018)
requirement: Satisfy the FSCA that controlling-body members and senior managers have the competency to undertake their duties and functions, including detailed knowledge of relevant OTC derivative structures, risks and markets; maintain an updated register of controlling-body members and senior managers; promptly notify the FSCA on termination of any appointment and the reason; submit Annexure B for each new appointment promptly; and annually submit a written statement to the FSCA confirming continued compliance with CS 1/2018 in respect of each controlling-body member and senior manager.
fulfilmentPolicy: Fit-and-Proper Policy; Competency Framework; ODP Authorisation Policy

section: Domain M-ODP-AUTH — ODP Authorisation Criteria (CS 1/2018)
requirement: Maintain the operational ability to fulfil all FMA responsibilities, including: a fixed business address in South Africa; adequate access to communication facilities including a full-time telephone or cell-phone service and administrative and electronic facilities; adequate storage and filing systems for safe-keeping of records and correspondence; and a bank account with a registered South African bank.
fulfilmentPolicy: ODP Authorisation Policy; Operational Resilience Policy

section: Domain M-ODP-AUTH — ODP Authorisation Criteria (CS 1/2018)
requirement: At all times: not be in liquidation, provisional liquidation, business rescue or creditor-arrangement; maintain assets (excluding goodwill and intangibles) exceeding liabilities (excluding validly subordinated loans); maintain current assets at least sufficient to meet current liabilities; not have any outstanding judgment debt; and ensure no controlling-body member or senior manager is an unrehabilitated insolvent, under debt review, or has an outstanding judgment debt.
fulfilmentPolicy: Governance Framework; Capital Management Policy

section: Domain M-ODP-AUTH — ODP Authorisation Criteria (CS 1/2018)
requirement: Organise and control affairs responsibly and effectively with sound risk-management principles and board-approved risk policies and processes; conduct an independent review of the risk-measurement system at least annually; maintain a compliance function staffed with competent individuals sufficiently independent from monitored activities; appoint a Head of Compliance responsible for the compliance function, FSCA reporting (annual and ad hoc on non-compliance and material irregularities), and oversight of FMA compliance; notify the FSCA of the Head of Compliance appointment; maintain a business continuity plan and regularly test it; and maintain proper, complete, accurate and secure records of all OTC derivative transaction instructions for at least six months after the instruction and of all contractual arrangements for at least five years after termination.
fulfilmentPolicy: Risk Management Framework; Compliance Policy; Business Continuity Plan; Records Management Policy

section: Domain M-ODP-COND — ODP Conduct Obligations (CS 2/2018)
requirement: Act at all times honestly, fairly, with due skill, care and diligence, and in the interests of clients, counterparties and market integrity; communicate information in a clear, fair and non-misleading way; manage conflicts of interest fairly; observe proper standards of market conduct; not impede the objects of the FMA; maintain knowledge of and comply with all applicable laws, rules and regulations; and engage with the FSCA in an open and cooperative way, disclosing any material non-compliance or material operational failure.
fulfilmentPolicy: Market Conduct Policy; Conflicts of Interest Policy; OTC Trading Policy

section: Domain M-ODP-COND — ODP Conduct Obligations (CS 2/2018)
requirement: Prior to entering into any OTC derivative transaction, categorise each person as counterparty or client; where a person meets the counterparty definition notify them in writing of their categorisation and its limitations; obtain written confirmation of awareness and agreement; assess appropriateness of counterparty categorisation where client elects up-categorisation; warn clients in writing of the implications of counterparty categorisation and clearing obligations; and re-categorise a counterparty back to client if they no longer meet counterparty requirements.
fulfilmentPolicy: Client Categorisation Policy; Counterparty Onboarding Policy

section: Domain M-ODP-COND — ODP Conduct Obligations (CS 2/2018)
requirement: Prior to executing an OTC derivative transaction with a client, request information regarding the client's financial situation, objectives, knowledge and experience in OTC derivatives to assess appropriateness for that product type; if the product is not appropriate notify the client in writing; if the client does not provide sufficient information warn the client in writing that appropriateness cannot be determined; maintain written policies and procedures for the appropriateness assessment.
fulfilmentPolicy: Conduct of Business and Treating Customers Fairly Policy §3.3; Counterparty Onboarding Policy

section: Domain M-ODP-COND — ODP Conduct Obligations (CS 2/2018)
requirement: Ensure all representations and information provided to clients are factually correct, in plain language, adequate and appropriate for the transaction or service, provided in good time before execution, in clear and readable format where written, and with all monetary amounts stated in specific monetary terms; provide material or significant changes in information without delay; provide a general explanation of the nature, material terms, restrictions, conditions and risks of each transaction sufficient for an informed client decision.
fulfilmentPolicy: Conduct of Business and Treating Customers Fairly Policy §3.9

section: Domain M-ODP-COND — ODP Conduct Obligations (CS 2/2018)
requirement: Enter into a written or electronic agreement with every client or counterparty covering: payment obligations, netting of payments, events of default and other termination events, calculation and netting of obligations upon termination and transfer, governing law, valuation of transactions, collateral and portfolios, and dispute resolution; the agreement must also make provision for confirmation arrangements (§8), credit-support arrangements including margin requirements and eligible collateral, collateral-safeguarding arrangements, counterparty-status attestation and notification obligations, client consent to trade-repository reporting, and the transaction-valuation process; maintain a record of all agreements and make them promptly available to the FSCA on request.
fulfilmentPolicy: Counterparty Onboarding Policy; Imani clause library; Collateral Management Policy

section: Domain M-ODP-COND — ODP Conduct Obligations (CS 2/2018)
requirement: Use best efforts to confirm every OTC derivative transaction by the end of the next business day for standard products or within five business days for complex products (per the schedule in Annexure A); maintain written policies and procedures for timely confirmation; make and retain records of the date and time of each transaction-supplement transmission and each confirmation; and provide the FSCA with a monthly report within 10 business days of month-end setting out, per product type and client or counterparty, the number of transactions not confirmed within the Annexure A timelines.
fulfilmentPolicy: Confirmation Procedure; OTC Trading Policy; Trade Reporting Policy

section: Domain M-ODP-COND — ODP Conduct Obligations (CS 2/2018)
requirement: Agree in writing with counterparties and clients on portfolio-reconciliation arrangements before entering into any OTC derivative contract; perform portfolio reconciliation at the frequency prescribed by portfolio size (counterparty: daily ≥500 trades, weekly 51–499, quarterly 1–50; client: quarterly ≥101, annually 1–100); maintain written policies and procedures for portfolio reconciliation; resolve material-term discrepancies within three business days and valuation discrepancies within five business days; deem unresolved discrepancies as disputes after those periods.
fulfilmentPolicy: Trade Confirmation and Affirmation Policy §3.3

section: Domain M-ODP-COND — ODP Conduct Obligations (CS 2/2018)
requirement: Maintain written policies and procedures for identifying, recording and monitoring disputes relating to material terms, recognition, valuation or collateral exchange; record the outstanding duration of each dispute, the counterparty or client and the disputed amount; resolve disputes in a timely manner with a specific escalation process for disputes not resolved within five business days; and promptly notify the FSCA of any dispute exceeding R100 million in transaction value that remains unresolved after 10 business days.
fulfilmentPolicy: OTC Dispute Resolution Procedure; Margin Policy

section: Domain M-ODP-COND — ODP Conduct Obligations (CS 2/2018)
requirement: Maintain written policies and procedures to analyse, at least twice a year, the possibility of conducting bilateral or multilateral portfolio compression on portfolios of 500 or more non-centrally cleared OTC derivative transactions with other providers; terminate fully offsetting transactions; keep a complete and accurate record of each bilateral offset and each bilateral or multilateral portfolio compression exercise; and be able to provide a reasonable and valid explanation to the FSCA if a compression exercise is assessed as not appropriate.
fulfilmentPolicy: Trade Confirmation and Affirmation Policy §3.4

section: Domain M-ODP-COND — ODP Conduct Obligations (CS 2/2018)
requirement: When receiving or holding client or counterparty funds or securities as collateral: observe utmost good faith, exercise proper care and diligence, and act in the best interests of the client or counterparty; segregate client and counterparty collateral from proprietary assets and ensure it is identifiable as such in the books of account; pay all client and counterparty funds into a separate account within one business day of receipt; ensure the separate account contains only client and counterparty funds, not those of the provider; and not cause securities to be registered other than in accordance with client or counterparty instructions.
fulfilmentPolicy: Collateral Management Policy; Safeguarding Procedure

section: Domain M-ODP-COND — ODP Conduct Obligations (CS 2/2018)
requirement: Where an intermediary markets or sells OTC derivatives to clients on the provider's behalf: ensure the intermediary is an FAIS-licensed FSP, discloses the arrangement and any fees in writing to clients, performs the §6 disclosure obligations and the §5 appropriateness test on behalf of the provider. All statements, advertisements and communications relating to OTC derivative business must be fair, clear, correct and not misleading or contrary to the public interest. All policies and procedures required by CS 2/2018 must be approved in writing by senior management. The provider may not induce any client or counterparty to waive any right conferred under CS 2/2018 and any such waiver is void.
fulfilmentPolicy: Conduct of Business and Treating Customers Fairly Policy §3.10

section: Domain M-ODP-COND — ODP Conduct Obligations (CS 2/2018)
requirement: Not disclose any information acquired or obtained from a counterparty or client except: where the person has given consent; where disclosure is required or permitted under law or a court order; where disclosure is necessary to carry out functions or duties under any law; or where disclosure is required for legal proceedings.
fulfilmentPolicy: Conduct of Business and Treating Customers Fairly Policy §3.11; POPIA Privacy Policy

section: Domain M-ODP-RPT — ODP Trade Reporting (CS 3/2018)
requirement: Report details of every executed, modified or terminated OTC derivative transaction — whether confirmed or not — in the following asset classes to the licensed trade repository: commodity derivatives, credit derivatives, foreign exchange derivatives, equity derivatives and interest rate derivatives.
fulfilmentPolicy: Trade Reporting Policy; ODP Authorisation Policy

section: Domain M-ODP-RPT — ODP Trade Reporting (CS 3/2018)
requirement: Where a trade is cleared through a CCP, the CCP bears the reporting obligation; where both counterparties are authorised ODPs, both bear the reporting obligation; the reporting obligation may be delegated. The report must contain at least the 100 data fields set out in Annexure A (items 1–100); reported data must be accurate; and a record of every derivative transaction and any modification must be kept for at least five years following termination.
fulfilmentPolicy: Trade Reporting Policy; Records Management Policy

section: Domain M-ODP-RPT — ODP Trade Reporting (CS 3/2018)
requirement: Submit the trade report by end of the next business day after execution, modification or termination; report mark-to-market or mark-to-model valuations daily based on the previous business day's closing market data; report any other Annexure A item 100 elements daily or as they occur; identify each reporting provider, non-reporting counterparty and CCP using an LEI (ISO 17442); identify each derivative instrument using a unique product identifier (UPI) meeting the nine international criteria; identify each transaction using a unique transaction identifier (UTI) allocated at the earliest point in the trade flow (reporting provider allocates UTI where both parties are ODPs; CCP allocates UTI where trade is cleared); generate UTIs to enable cross-repository data aggregation.
fulfilmentPolicy: Trade Reporting Policy; LEI Management Procedure; UTI Allocation Procedure

section: Domain M-ODP-RPT — ODP Trade Reporting (CS 3/2018)
citation: CS 3/2018 Annexure A items 1–59 (counterparty, product and transaction data fields)
requirement: Report to the licensed trade repository — for each OTC derivative transaction — the following data field clusters: **(a) Counterparty data (items 1–11):** reporting timestamp (UTC); reporting-counterparty LEI or unique client code; non-reporting counterparty ID type and LEI/BIC; nature (F/N/C/O) and corporate sector of reporting counterparty; broker ID; country of non-reporting counterparty (ISO 3166); trading capacity (principal/agent); counterparty side (buyer/seller); and submitting-entity LEI. **(b) Product and transaction data (items 12–28):** unique product identifier; beneficiary type and ID; inter-affiliate indicator; collateralisation type (FC/PC/OC/U); collateral portfolio code; initial margin posted/received and currency; variation margin posted/received and currency; contract type (CD/FR/FU/FW/OP/SB/SW/ST/OT); underlying-asset identifiers 1 and 2 (ISO 6166); asset class (IR/CR/CO/CU/Equity); UTI; and complex-trade component identifier. **(c) Transaction details (items 29–58):** electronic-trading-venue LEI; effective, maturity, termination and settlement dates (ISO 8601); master agreement type and version; payment and reset frequency; day count convention; delivery type; price 1 and 2 with notation type and multiplier; notional currencies 1 and 2 and settlement currency; up-front payment amount and currency; embedded-option indicator; confirmation status and timestamp; clearing timestamp; cleared indicator and CCP LEI; clearing-member name and LEI; clearing exemption; and intragroup indicator.
fulfilmentPolicy: Trade Reporting Policy; Anya schema-registry; Strate TR connectivity

section: Domain M-ODP-RPT — ODP Trade Reporting (CS 3/2018)
citation: CS 3/2018 Annexure A items 60–100 (asset-class specific and event/valuation data fields)
requirement: Report to the licensed trade repository the following additional data field clusters for each OTC derivative transaction: **(a) Interest rate derivative fields (items 60–67):** fixed rate for legs 1 and 2; floating rate for legs 1 and 2; fixed-rate day count convention for legs 1 and 2; fixed/floating-leg payment frequency; floating-rate reset frequency (MNTH/QURT/MIAN/YEAR). **(b) Currency derivative fields (items 68–71):** exchange rate; delivery currency 2; forward exchange rate; exchange-rate basis. **(c) Commodity derivative fields (items 72–76):** commodity sub-asset class; quantity and unit of measure; grade of product; delivery point. **(d) Credit derivative fields (items 77–88):** buyer/seller counterparty ID and name; reference entity; index attachment/detachment points; payment frequency; calculation basis; index factor; tranche indicator; series number. **(e) Option fields (items 89–93):** option exercise date; option premium; strike price (cap/floor rate); option exercise style; option type (Put/Call). **(f) Event and valuation data (items 94–100):** action code (N=New, M=Modify, E=Error, C=Early Termination, R=Correction, Z=Compression, V=Valuation update, P=Position component); execution timestamp (UTC); reporting timestamp (UTC); contract value (MTM or mark-to-model; CCP valuation for cleared trades); valuation currency; valuation date; and other details (free text for terms not captured in prescribed fields).
fulfilmentPolicy: Trade Reporting Policy; Anya schema-registry; Valuation Procedure

section: Domain A-OR-RESILIENCE — Operational Resilience (D4/2023)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D4/2023** §2.1.1 + §1.3. `§2.1.1: Banks must assess the adequacy and robustness of their current policies, processes and practices against the principles for operational resilience issued by the BCBS. §1.3: The principles are required to be applied on a consolidated basis and also form an integral part of a bank's forward-looking operational resilience approach in line with its operational risk appetite and tolerance for disruption.` BCBS Principles for Operational Resilience (March 2021, https://www.bis.org/bcbs/publ/d516.htm). Enabling authority: Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a); Reg 39 (operational risk management process).
requirement: Assess the adequacy and robustness of current policies, processes and practices against the BCBS Principles for Operational Resilience (March 2021), applying the assessment on a consolidated basis and integrating it with the bank's forward-looking operational resilience approach in line with its risk appetite and tolerance for disruption.
fulfilmentPolicy: Operational Resilience Policy; Risk Management Framework; `Procedures/by-policy/operational-resilience.md` (planned)

section: Domain A-OR-RESILIENCE — Operational Resilience (D4/2023)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D4/2023** §2.1.2. `§2.1.2: All operational resilience controls implemented by the bank must follow a risk-based approach that is aligned with the bank's risk appetite, based on the nature, size and complexity of its operations.` Reg 38(4) (PA power to require capital or policy alignment where operational resilience policies are inadequate).
requirement: Implement all operational resilience controls following a risk-based approach that is aligned with the bank's board-approved risk appetite, calibrated to the nature, size, and complexity of the bank's operations.
fulfilmentPolicy: Operational Resilience Policy; Risk Appetite Statement; Operational Risk Policy

section: Domain A-OR-RESILIENCE — Operational Resilience (D4/2023)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D4/2023** §2.1.3 + §1.2.1–§1.2.7. `§2.1.3: Banks must ensure that all principles contained in the BCBS paper are addressed either through internal resources or by means of outsourcing/third party agreements without undue delay.` The seven BCBS principle categories per §1.2.1–§1.2.7: (1) governance; (2) operational risk management; (3) business continuity planning and testing; (4) mapping of interconnections and interdependencies of critical operations; (5) third-party dependency management; (6) incident management; (7) resilient information and communication technology (ICT), including cyber security.
requirement: Address all seven BCBS Operational Resilience principle categories — governance; operational risk management; business continuity planning and testing; mapping of interconnections and interdependencies of critical operations; third-party dependency management; incident management; and resilient ICT including cyber security — through internal resources or outsourcing/third-party agreements, without undue delay.
fulfilmentPolicy: Operational Resilience Policy; Business Continuity Plan; Third-Party Risk Management Policy; Incident Management Procedure; IT/ICT Security Policy

section: Domain A-OR-RESILIENCE — Operational Resilience (D4/2023)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D4/2023** §2.1.4. `§2.1.4: Existing risk management frameworks, business continuity plans and third-party dependency management must be implemented consistently within the bank.` Reg 39 (requirement for comprehensive risk management processes, practices and procedures and board-approved policies).
requirement: Implement existing risk management frameworks, business continuity plans, and third-party dependency management consistently across the entire bank organisation.
fulfilmentPolicy: Operational Resilience Policy; Operational Risk Policy; Business Continuity Plan; Third-Party Risk Management Policy

section: Domain A-OR-RESILIENCE — Operational Resilience (D4/2023)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D4/2023** §2.1.5. `§2.1.5: Banks must consider whether its operational resilience approach is appropriately harmonised with the stated actions, organisational mappings, and definitions of critical functions and critical shared services contained in its recovery and resolution plans.` PA Directive 1 of 2015 (recovery plan minimum requirements, `ORG-PR-35`).
requirement: Assess whether the operational resilience approach is appropriately harmonised with the recovery and resolution plans' stated actions, organisational mappings, and definitions of critical functions and critical shared services; align where gaps are identified.
fulfilmentPolicy: Operational Resilience Policy; Recovery and Resolution Plan; Business Continuity Plan

section: Domain A-OR-RESILIENCE — Operational Resilience (D4/2023)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D4/2023** §2.2 + §3 (Acknowledgement of receipt). `§2.2: All banks must comply with the respective requirements specified in this directive on or before 31 December 2024.` `§3: Kindly ensure that a copy of this Directive is made available to your institution's external auditors. In addition, the attached acknowledgement of receipt, duly completed and signed by both the Chief Executive Officer of the institution and the said auditors, should be returned to the PA at the earliest convenience of the signatories.` Issued by Fundi Tshazibana, Chief Executive Officer, Date: 01/06/23.
requirement: Comply with all requirements of Directive D4/2023 by 31 December 2024; provide a copy of the directive to external auditors; return the completed acknowledgement of receipt, signed by the Chief Executive Officer and the external auditors, to the Prudential Authority at the earliest convenience.
fulfilmentPolicy: Operational Resilience Policy; Regulatory Engagement Policy

section: Domain D — Privacy and data protection
citation: POPIA 4/2013 s.11
requirement: Process personal information only where a lawful basis exists under POPIA s.11 — consent, contractual necessity, legal obligation, protection of a legitimate interest, public-law duty, or the responsible party's or a third party's legitimate interest. Record the lawful basis relied upon for each processing operation.
fulfilmentPolicy: POPIA Privacy Policy

section: Domain D — Privacy and data protection
citation: POPIA s.13
requirement: Collect and process personal information for a specific, explicitly defined and lawful purpose related to the bank's functions under POPIA s.13, and document that purpose. Do not process for purposes incompatible with the one for which the information was collected.
fulfilmentPolicy: POPIA Privacy Policy; Lawful-Processing Register

section: Domain D — Privacy and data protection
citation: POPIA s.14
requirement: Retain personal information only for as long as necessary to achieve the purpose for which it was collected, or as required by law, under POPIA s.14, and operate a documented retention-and-deletion schedule. Securely destroy or de-identify information once the retention basis falls away.
fulfilmentPolicy: Data Retention & Disposal Policy; Records Management Policy

section: Domain D — Privacy and data protection
citation: POPIA s.15
requirement: Ensure any further processing of personal information is compatible with the purpose for which it was originally collected under POPIA s.15, assessing compatibility against the relationship, nature, consequences and any contractual or legal basis. Obtain a fresh lawful basis where further processing is not compatible.
fulfilmentPolicy: POPIA Privacy Policy

section: Domain D — Privacy and data protection
citation: POPIA s.18
requirement: Notify data subjects of the prescribed particulars when collecting their personal information under POPIA s.18 — including the information collected, the purpose, the recipients, and the data subject's rights — unless an exemption applies. Provide the notice before or as soon as reasonably practicable after collection.
fulfilmentPolicy: POPIA Privacy Policy; Consent & Notice Policy

section: Domain D — Privacy and data protection
citation: POPIA ss.19–22
requirement: Secure the integrity and confidentiality of personal information under POPIA ss.19–22 by maintaining appropriate, reasonable technical and organisational measures against loss, damage, unauthorised destruction, and unlawful access or processing, informed by generally accepted security practices and the bank's risk assessment. Impose equivalent obligations on operators (processors) by written contract.
fulfilmentPolicy: Information Security Policy; POPIA Privacy Policy

section: Domain D — Privacy and data protection
citation: POPIA s.22

section: Domain D — Privacy and data protection

fulfilmentPolicy: POPIA Privacy Policy; Data Subject Rights workflow

citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D1/2022** §1.2 + §2.3. `§1.2: The LCR promotes short-term resilience of banks' exposure to liquidity risk by ensuring that they have sufficient unencumbered high-quality liquid assets (HQLA) that can be easily and immediately converted into cash in private markets to meet their liquidity needs for a 30 calendar-day liquidity stress scenario. §2.3: Consolidation within this context should be read in conjunction with the objective of the LCR, which is to ensure that every bank maintains an adequate stock of HQLA to meet its liquidity needs for a 30 calendar-day liquidity stress scenario.` Regulations Relating to Banks Reg 26(12).

section: Domain PR-LCR — Liquidity Coverage Ratio: Scope of Application and Calculation (D1/2022)

section: Domain PR-LCR — Liquidity Coverage Ratio: Scope of Application and Calculation (D1/2022)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D1/2022** §4.1.2.5. `§4.1.2.5: a summation of the relevant individual net cash outflows and the HQLA portfolios of all the relevant entities shall be performed in order to calculate the relevant required consolidated LCR. In this regard, the HQLA of the relevant entities shall be capped at the lower of the specified minimum LCR requirement in each relevant jurisdiction or the home jurisdiction in the summation process. Any excess HQLA or inflows of a particular entity shall only be included in the consolidated LCR once it has been evaluated for transferability across jurisdictions and convertibility across currencies, and if it is freely available to the consolidated (parent) entity in times of stress.`
requirement: Sum net cash outflows and HQLA portfolios of all consolidated entities to calculate the consolidated LCR; cap entity-level HQLA at the lower of the minimum LCR requirement in the relevant jurisdiction or the home jurisdiction; include excess HQLA or inflows in the consolidated LCR only if evaluated as freely transferable across jurisdictions and convertible across currencies and available to the parent entity in stress.
fulfilmentPolicy: Liquidity Risk Management Policy; LCR Policy; HQLA Management Policy

section: Domain PR-NSFR — Net Stable Funding Ratio: Calibration and Implementation (D1/2023)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D1/2023** §2.2.1–§2.2.3. `§2.2.1: The amount of ASF is measured based on the broad characteristics of the relative stability of an institution's funding sources, including the contractual maturity of its liabilities and the differences in the propensity of different types of funding providers to withdraw their funding. §2.2.2: The ASF's calibration presupposes that long-term funding is more stable than short-term funding. §2.2.3: The NSFR framework assumes that regulatory capital and funding provided by retail and small business customers are the most stable sources of funding and have the highest ASF factors assigned to them.` Regulations Relating to Banks Reg 26(14).
requirement: Measure the Available Stable Funding (ASF) based on the stability characteristics of funding sources, applying the ASF factor hierarchy: regulatory capital and retail/small business deposits carry the highest ASF factors; long-term funding receives higher ASF factors than short-term funding.
fulfilmentPolicy: Liquidity Risk Management Policy; NSFR Policy; Capital Management Policy

section: Domain PR-NSFR — Net Stable Funding Ratio: Calibration and Implementation (D1/2023)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D1/2023** §2.2.4. `§2.2.4: Funding with a residual maturity of less than one year received from non-financial corporate customers, sovereigns and public-sector entities, as well as funding from financial corporate customers with a residual maturity of between six months and one year, shall be assigned an ASF factor of 50 per cent.`
requirement: Assign an ASF factor of 50% to: (a) funding with residual maturity of less than one year from non-financial corporate customers, sovereigns, and public-sector entities; and (b) funding from financial corporate customers with residual maturity between six months and one year.
fulfilmentPolicy: Liquidity Risk Management Policy; NSFR Policy

section: Domain PR-NSFR — Net Stable Funding Ratio: Calibration and Implementation (D1/2023)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D1/2023** §2.2.5. `§2.2.5: The NSFR framework assigns an ASF factor of zero per cent to funding with a residual maturity of less than six months from financial corporate customers. The PA concluded in 2017 that it would be appropriate to deviate from the international standard and to assign an ASF factor of 35 per cent to secured and unsecured funding received in Rand (ZAR) from financial corporate customers, excluding banks, with a residual maturity of less than six months. This dispensation was only available for banks conducting business in South Africa. In order to be fully compliant with the NSFR framework, the PA has decided to phase out the ASF factor in this regard as follows: Table 1 Period ASF Percentage From 1 June 2023 to 31 December 2023 30 From 1 January 2024 to 31 December 2024 20 From 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2027 10 From 1 January 2028 onwards 0.`
requirement: Apply the phased ASF factor for secured and unsecured ZAR funding from financial corporate customers (excluding banks) with residual maturity < 6 months, according to the D1/2023 phase-out table: 30% (1 June 2023 – 31 Dec 2023); 20% (1 Jan 2024 – 31 Dec 2024); 10% (1 Jan 2025 – 31 Dec 2027); 0% (from 1 Jan 2028). The international standard of 0% applies to all other currencies and from 1 January 2028 onwards.
fulfilmentPolicy: Liquidity Risk Management Policy; NSFR Policy

section: Domain PR-NSFR — Net Stable Funding Ratio: Calibration and Implementation (D1/2023)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D1/2023** §2.3.1–§2.3.2. `§2.3.1: The amount of RSF is measured based on the broad characteristics of the liquidity risk profile of an institution's assets and off-balance sheet (OBS) exposures. §2.3.2: The RSF considers the need for resilient credit extension, bank behaviour, liquidity value, asset tenor and asset quality. Accordingly, the PA's assessment that the RSF factors set out in the NSFR framework is appropriate and shall be implemented accordingly by banks.` Regulations Relating to Banks Reg 26(14).
requirement: Measure Required Stable Funding (RSF) based on the liquidity risk profile of assets and off-balance sheet exposures; implement the RSF factors set out in the BCBS NSFR framework as calibrated for South Africa by the PA, taking into account resilient credit extension, bank behaviour, liquidity value, asset tenor, and asset quality.
fulfilmentPolicy: Liquidity Risk Management Policy; NSFR Policy; Asset and Liability Management Policy

requirement: Make a copy of Directive D1/2024 available to the institution's auditors and return the duly completed and signed acknowledgement of receipt — signed by both the Chief Executive Officer and the auditors — to the Prudential Authority.
fulfilmentPolicy: Regulatory Engagement Policy; External Audit Policy

section: Domain PR-P3 — Pillar 3 Disclosure: Interest Rate Risk in the Banking Book (D1/2024)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D1/2024** §1.3. `§1.3: This directive remains effective as confirmed in Banks Act Circular 1 of the relevant year.` The directive's effectiveness is re-confirmed annually via the PA's Banks Act Circular 1, requiring the bank to monitor annual circulars for any amendments or withdrawals of the IRRBB Pillar 3 disclosure requirements. Enabling authority: Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a).
requirement: Monitor and comply with Banks Act Circular 1 of each relevant year to confirm the continued effectiveness of Directive D1/2024, and implement any amendments to the IRRBB Pillar 3 disclosure requirements as notified by the Prudential Authority.
fulfilmentPolicy: Regulatory Change Management Policy; IRRBB Policy

section: Domain A-PVA — Prudent Valuation Adjustments (D5/2020)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D5/2020** §2.1 — Individual PVA consideration obligation. `§2.1: Banks have to consider all PVAs individually (that is, regardless of the ability to associate them with a single PVA group or category). However, banks may estimate PVAs in line with internal governance models. Banks must, at a minimum, consider the following PVAs: [§2.1.1 Investing and funding costs; §2.1.2 Close-out uncertainty (mid-market value, close-out cost, concentration); §2.1.3 Unearned credit spreads; §2.1.4 Early termination; §2.1.5 Model risk; §2.1.6 Operational risk; §2.1.7 Future administrative costs; §2.1.8 Other; §2.1.9 DVA excluded].` Reg 39(13)(c)(i)(D) (PVA categories in the Regulations).
requirement: Consider all PVAs individually for all fair-valued positions at a minimum across the eight prescribed categories: investing and funding costs; close-out uncertainty (mid-market value, close-out cost, concentration); unearned credit spreads; early termination; model risk; operational risk; future administrative costs; and other; noting that Debit Valuation Adjustments (DVA) are excluded from individual PVAs.
fulfilmentPolicy: Valuation Policy; Market Risk Policy; Capital Management Policy

section: Domain A-PVA — Prudent Valuation Adjustments (D5/2020)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D5/2020** Annexure A §2.1.1.1 — Materiality threshold for simplified vs core approach. `§2.1.1.1: The simplified approach can only be adopted where the total adjustments to fair values that affect CET 1 as a percentage of the sum of the absolute value of fair-valued assets and liabilities (excluding DVA) is below 1%. For fair-valued assets and liabilities whose adjustments to fair values has a partial or zero impact on CET 1 capital, their values must only be included to the extent of the impact on CET 1. Exactly matching, offsetting fair valued assets and liabilities are excluded. §2.1.1.3: This materiality threshold must be applied at the following levels: bank solo, bank consolidated, controlling company consolidated, foreign branch and foreign subsidiary. Where the threshold is breached at controlling company level, the core approach must be applied at all levels in the banking group.`
requirement: Apply the materiality threshold test to determine whether the simplified or core approach applies for PVA calculation: if total fair-value adjustments affecting CET1, as a percentage of absolute fair-valued assets and liabilities (excluding DVA), is below 1%, the simplified approach is permitted; if the threshold is breached at any level — including controlling-company consolidated — the core approach must be applied at all levels in the banking group.
fulfilmentPolicy: Valuation Policy; Capital Management Policy

section: Domain A-PVA — Prudent Valuation Adjustments (D5/2020)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D5/2020** Annexure A §3.1–§3.3 — Simplified approach calculation. `§3.1: Banks must calculate the PVA under the simplified approach as 0.1% of the sum of absolute value of fair-valued assets and liabilities which are included in the materiality threshold calculation in paragraph 2.1.1 above. §3.2: the aggregate PVA must be the PVA resulting from the calculation in §3.1. §3.3: for Pillar 3 disclosure requirements and Template PV1, the aggregate PVA from the calculation in §3.1 must be allocated to individual PVA categories.` + D5/2020 §2.3: follow Annexure A requirements for individual PVA determination.
requirement: Where the simplified approach applies (materiality threshold < 1%), calculate the aggregate PVA as 0.1% of the sum of the absolute value of fair-valued assets and liabilities; allocate the aggregate PVA to individual PVA categories for Pillar 3 Template PV1 disclosure.
fulfilmentPolicy: Valuation Policy; Pillar 3 Disclosure Policy

section: Domain A-PVA — Prudent Valuation Adjustments (D5/2020)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D5/2020** Annexure A §4.1.1–§4.2.4 — Core approach — general provisions. `§4.1.1: Banks must calculate PVAs under the core approach by: (a) calculating PVAs for each category described in Reg 39(13)(c)(i)(D); (b) summing category-level PVAs to provide the aggregate PVA. §4.2.1: For fair-valued assets and liabilities where accounting valuation change has partial or zero impact on CET1 capital, PVAs must only be calculated based on the proportion impacting CET1 (excludes DVA already deducted). §4.2.3: PVAs must be excess of valuation adjustments required to achieve prudent value over adjustments applied in fair value addressing the same source of valuation uncertainty. §4.2.4: PVAs must always be positive, including at valuation exposure level, category level, both pre- and post-aggregation.` Reg 39(13)(c)(i)(D) (PVA categories).
requirement: Under the core approach, calculate PVAs for each prescribed PVA category per Reg 39(13)(c)(i)(D), then sum category-level PVAs to the aggregate; ensure PVAs are always positive at valuation exposure level and category level; calculate only the proportion of PVA impacting CET1 for assets where accounting fair-value change has partial or zero CET1 impact.
fulfilmentPolicy: Valuation Policy; Capital Management Policy

section: Domain A-PVA — Prudent Valuation Adjustments (D5/2020)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D5/2020** Annexure A §4.3.1–§4.3.6 — Mid-market value PVA calculation. `§4.3.1: Mid-market value PVAs must be calculated at valuation exposure level. §4.3.2: The mid-market value PVA must only be assessed to have zero value where: (a) the bank has firm evidence of a tradable price for a valuation exposure or reliable data based on a liquid market; and (b) market data sources do not indicate any material valuation uncertainty. §4.3.3: Where a valuation exposure cannot be shown to have zero PVA, banks must use market data sources when assessing the mid-market value PVA. §4.3.6: Banks must calculate the total category level PVA for mid-market value by applying to individual mid-market value PVAs the formulae for either Method 1 or Method 2 per Exhibit 1.`
requirement: Calculate mid-market value PVAs at valuation exposure level for all fair-valued positions; assess zero mid-market value PVA only where both conditions are met (firm tradable price evidence and no material valuation uncertainty); aggregate using Method 1 or Method 2 formulae from Exhibit 1 of Annexure A.
fulfilmentPolicy: Valuation Policy; Independent Price Verification Procedure

section: Domain A-PVA — Prudent Valuation Adjustments (D5/2020)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D5/2020** Annexure A §4.4.1–§4.4.7 — Close-out cost PVA calculation. `§4.4.1: Close-out cost PVAs must be calculated at valuation exposure level. §4.4.3: The close-out cost PVA may be assessed to have zero value on condition that the bank provides evidence that it is 90% confident that sufficient liquidity exists to support the exit of the related valuation exposures at mid-price. §4.4.7: Banks must calculate the total category level PVA for close-out cost by applying to the individual close-out cost PVAs the formulae for either Method 1 or Method 2 per Exhibit 1.`
requirement: Calculate close-out cost PVAs at valuation exposure level; assess zero close-out cost PVA only where the bank has 90% confidence that sufficient liquidity exists to support exit at mid-price; aggregate using Method 1 or Method 2 from Exhibit 1 of Annexure A.
fulfilmentPolicy: Valuation Policy; Liquidity Risk Management Policy

section: Domain A-PVA — Prudent Valuation Adjustments (D5/2020)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D5/2020** Annexure A §4.5.1–§4.5.6 — Model risk PVA calculation. `§4.5.1: Where appropriate, banks must estimate a model risk PVA for each valuation model by considering valuation model risk which arises due to the potential existence of a range of different models or model calibrations, which are used by market participants, and the lack of a firm exit price for the specific product being valued. Banks must not consider valuation model risk which arises due to calibrations from market derived parameters (must be captured in mid-market value PVA). §4.5.5: Where banks use a specific method, the prudence must be confirmed annually by comparison to an alternative approach on a material sample of valuation models. §4.5.6: Banks must calculate the total category level PVA for model risk by applying to individual model risk PVAs the formulae for either Method 1 or Method 2 per Exhibit 1.`
requirement: Estimate a model risk PVA for each valuation model covering: range of models/calibrations used by market participants; lack of firm exit price; not including market-derived-parameter risk (captured in mid-market PVA); confirm the prudence of the chosen method annually for a material sample; aggregate using Method 1 or Method 2 from Exhibit 1.
fulfilmentPolicy: Valuation Policy; Model Risk Policy

section: Domain A-PVA — Prudent Valuation Adjustments (D5/2020)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D5/2020** Annexure A §4.6.1–§4.6.2 — Unearned credit spreads PVA. `§4.6.1: Banks must calculate the unearned credit spreads PVA to reflect the valuation uncertainty in the adjustment necessary, in accordance with the applicable accounting framework, to include the present value of expected losses due to counterparty default on derivative positions, discounted using a rate which approximate the risk-free rate. This PVA must be considered at counterparty level. §4.6.2: Banks must include the element of the PVA relating to mid-market value within the mid-market value PVA category; the element relating to close-out cost uncertainty within the close-out costs PVA category; the element relating to model risk within the model risk PVA category.`
requirement: Calculate the unearned credit spreads PVA at counterparty level to reflect valuation uncertainty in CVA (present value of expected losses from counterparty default, discounted at risk-free rate); decompose the unearned credit spreads PVA elements across mid-market value, close-out cost, and model risk PVA categories.
fulfilmentPolicy: Valuation Policy; Credit Risk Policy; Capital Management Policy

section: Domain A-PVA — Prudent Valuation Adjustments (D5/2020)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D5/2020** Annexure A §4.8.1–§4.8.3 — Concentration PVA. `§4.8.1: Banks must estimate a concentration PVA for concentrated valuation positions by applying the following three-step approach: (a) identify concentrated valuation positions; (b) for each identified concentrated valuation position where market price for size is unavailable, estimate a prudent exit period; (c) only where the prudent exit period exceeds 10 days, estimate a PVA taking into account volatility of the valuation input, volatility of the bid-offer spread, and impact of hypothetical exit strategy on market prices. §4.8.2: Identification must consider: size of positions relative to market liquidity; the institution's ability to trade in that market; average daily market volume and typical daily trading volume of the bank. §4.8.3: Banks must establish and document the methodology for determining concentrated positions.`
requirement: Estimate a concentration PVA for concentrated valuation positions using the three-step approach (identification, prudent exit period estimation, PVA calculation for positions with exit period > 10 days); document the concentration-identification methodology considering relative position size, market liquidity, and trading volumes.
fulfilmentPolicy: Valuation Policy; Market Risk Policy; Independent Price Verification Procedure

section: Domain A-PVA — Prudent Valuation Adjustments (D5/2020)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D5/2020** Annexure A §4.9.1–§4.9.4 — Future administrative costs PVA. `§4.9.2: Where a valuation exposure cannot be shown to have zero PVA per §4.9.1, banks must calculate the future administrative cost PVA considering administrative costs and future hedging costs over the expected life of valuation exposures for which a direct exit price is not applied for close-out costs, discounted at a rate approximating the risk-free rate. §4.9.3: Administrative costs must include all incremental staffing and fixed costs that will be incurred in managing the portfolio. §4.9.4: Banks must calculate the total category level PVA for future administrative costs as the sum of individual future administrative costs PVAs.`
requirement: Calculate future administrative cost PVAs for valuation exposures where close-out cost PVA is non-zero, covering administrative and future hedging costs over the expected portfolio life (discounted at risk-free rate), including all incremental staffing and fixed costs; sum individual future administrative cost PVAs to the category-level aggregate.
fulfilmentPolicy: Valuation Policy; Capital Management Policy

section: Domain A-PVA — Prudent Valuation Adjustments (D5/2020)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D5/2020** Annexure A §4.11.1 — Operational risk PVA and IPV process requirement. `§4.11.1: Banks must estimate a PVA for operational risk to be zero, provided that the bank has a defined IPV process which is audited both internally and externally, and the audit outcome of the IPV process has indicated no material process failure. Where the bank does not have a defined IPV process which is audited both internally and externally or the audit outcome has indicated a material process failure, the bank must calculate an operational risk PVA as 10% of the sum of the aggregated category level PVAs for mid-market value and close-out costs.`
requirement: Maintain a defined independent price verification (IPV) process that is audited both internally and externally with no material process failure, in order to assess zero operational risk PVA; where no such IPV process exists or where a material process failure is found by audit, calculate the operational risk PVA as 10% of the sum of aggregated category-level PVAs for mid-market value and close-out costs.
fulfilmentPolicy: Valuation Policy; Internal Audit Policy; Independent Price Verification Procedure

section: Domain A-PVA — Prudent Valuation Adjustments (D5/2020)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D5/2020** §4.1–§4.3 (Reporting and disclosure obligations, directive body). `§4.1: The aggregate PVA must be reported in line item 203 of the form BA 700. §4.2: Banks must estimate their PVAs at least on a quarterly basis. The PVA must be disclosed annually, in accordance with Directive 1 of 2019. Rows which are not applicable to the reporting bank must be completed as zero ('0') and the reason why they are not applicable must be explained in the accompanying narrative. §4.3: The PVAs must be estimated at bank solo, bank consolidated, controlling company consolidated and branches as well as subsidiaries of local banks. The rationale behind estimating at consolidated level is to minimise any arbitrage of the framework through the use of complex organisation structures, which could be cross jurisdictional.` **substrate-note (BA 700 line-number mapping):** D5/2020 §4.1 maps the aggregate PVA to **BA 700 line item 203**. The BA 700 renderer should resolve `BA700:line_203` to this obligation.
requirement: Report the aggregate PVA in BA 700 line item 203; estimate PVAs at least quarterly; disclose PVAs annually in accordance with Directive 1 of 2019 (Pillar 3); complete non-applicable rows with zero and explanatory narrative; estimate PVAs at bank solo, bank consolidated, controlling-company consolidated, and branch/subsidiary levels to prevent cross-jurisdictional arbitrage.
fulfilmentPolicy: Valuation Policy; Regulatory Reporting Policy; Pillar 3 Disclosure Policy; Capital Management Policy

section: Domain PR-REP43 — Auditor Reporting Requirements under Regulation 46 (D2/2024)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D2/2024** §1.1–§1.2 + Directive §2.1.1. `§1.1: Regulation 46(1) of the Regulations requires the auditor of a bank to report annually, within 120 days of the financial year end, on the bank's financial position and the results of its operations, as reflected in the regulatory returns specified in regulation 46(6) of the Regulations. §1.2: In addition to reporting on the quantitative aspects, the auditor is also required to report on qualitative aspects of the bank and its operations, including, but not limited to the bank's system of internal controls. §2.1.1: To perform an audit, review or limited assurance engagement on the respective regulatory returns specified in regulation 46(6) of the Regulations, in accordance with the detailed audit matrix provided in Annexure 1 for reports submitted to the PA in relation to engagements for financial years ended on or after 30 September 2023.` Regulations Relating to Banks Reg 46(1) (annual auditor report within 120 days) + Reg 46(6) (audit matrix — returns subject to audit/review/limited assurance).
requirement: Ensure the bank's appointed auditor performs an audit, review, or limited assurance engagement on the regulatory returns specified in Reg 46(6) in accordance with the D2/2024 Annexure 1 audit matrix, and submits the resulting report to the Prudential Authority within 120 days of the bank's financial year end — covering both quantitative BA returns and qualitative aspects including the bank's system of internal controls.
fulfilmentPolicy: Regulatory Reporting Policy (planned); External Audit Policy; Capital Management Policy; `Procedures/by-policy/ba-returns-regulation-46.md` (planned)

section: Domain PR-REP43 — Auditor Reporting Requirements under Regulation 46 (D2/2024)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D2/2024** §1.3–§1.5 + Directive §2.1.2–§2.1.3. `§1.3: Regulation 46(6) of the Regulations further requires that the auditor's reports contemplated in the same regulation be rendered in accordance with the wording and practices agreed from time to time between the Prudential Authority (PA), the South African Institute of Chartered Accountants and the Independent Regulatory Board for Auditors (IRBA). §1.5: In respect of regulatory reports pertaining to South African operations, the illustrative regulatory reports referenced above comprise Parts A to I, with Parts A to E addressing the reports required in terms of regulation 46(6) of the Regulations: Part A – Audit report on the year-end BA returns; Part B – Review report on the year-end BA returns; Part C – Limited assurance report on risk returns at year-end; Part D – Limited assurance report on risk returns at year-end derived from internal models; Part E – Limited assurance report on BA 325 daily market risk returns. §2.1.2: The reports submitted to the PA, in relation to the above, shall be rendered in accordance with the illustrative regulatory reports published by the IRBA from time to time. §2.1.3: Parts A to E and Parts A to D of the respective reports submitted to the PA shall make reference to this Directive insofar as the detail of audit, review or limited assurance work performed is concerned.` Reg 46(6) (agreed wording with PA/SAICA/IRBA).
requirement: Ensure that auditor reports on SA-operations BA returns are rendered in accordance with the current IRBA illustrative regulatory reports (Parts A to E for SA operations) — incorporating Part A (audit), Part B (review), Part C (limited assurance risk returns), Part D (limited assurance risk returns from internal models), and Part E (limited assurance BA 325 daily market risk returns) — and that all submitted reports expressly reference Directive D2/2024 regarding the scope of audit, review, or limited assurance work performed.
fulfilmentPolicy: External Audit Policy; Regulatory Reporting Policy; Capital Management Policy

section: Domain A-SACCR — SA-CCR Granular Obligations (D7/2020)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D7/2020** §2.1 — Core SA-CCR exposure formula. `§2.1: banks are hereby directed to calculate its exposures associated with all derivative transactions, including where a bank sells protection using a credit derivative, through the application of the formula: Exposure amount = alpha × (RC + PFE), where alpha = 1.4; RC = replacement cost; PFE = potential future exposure.` Enabling authority: Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a); Regulations Relating to Banks Reg 38A (leverage ratio).
requirement: Calculate the leverage ratio derivative exposure amount for all derivative transactions using the SA-CCR formula: Exposure = 1.4 × (RC + PFE), where RC is the replacement cost and PFE is the potential future exposure, as directed by D7/2020 §2.1 simultaneously with implementation of the amended Regulations.
fulfilmentPolicy: Capital Management Policy; Market Risk Policy; `Procedures/by-policy/leverage-ratio-sa-ccr.md` (planned)

requirement: Where derivative exposures are covered by an eligible bilateral netting contract complying with Reg 23(18)(b), calculate the exposure for the netting set as the sum of net mark-to-market replacement cost plus PFE, applying the SA-CCR netting methodology.
fulfilmentPolicy: Capital Management Policy; Collateral Management Policy; Netting Legal Framework

section: Domain A-SACCR — SA-CCR Granular Obligations (D7/2020)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D7/2020** §2.3.1 — Prohibition on netting collateral received against leverage exposure. `§2.3.1: Since collateral received in respect of any derivative contract does not necessarily reduce the leverage inherent in a bank's derivatives position, the bank shall not apply any netting between the collateral received and the bank's derivative exposure, irrespective of whether or not netting may be permitted in terms of the bank's operative accounting or risk-based framework provided for in the Regulations; whenever the bank calculates its relevant exposure amount, the bank shall not reduce the exposure amount by any collateral received from the counterparty.`
requirement: When calculating the leverage ratio derivative exposure amount, not reduce the exposure amount by any collateral received from the counterparty, regardless of whether netting is permitted under the bank's accounting or risk-based framework.
fulfilmentPolicy: Capital Management Policy; Collateral Management Policy; `Procedures/by-policy/leverage-ratio-sa-ccr.md` (planned)

section: Domain A-SACCR — SA-CCR Granular Obligations (D7/2020)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D7/2020** §2.3.2 — Gross-up for collateral provided. `§2.3.2: Whenever the bank provides collateral, the bank shall gross up its relevant exposure measure by the amount of any derivatives collateral so provided when the provision of such collateral reduces the value of the bank's balance sheet assets in terms of its relevant operative accounting framework.`
requirement: When the bank provides derivatives collateral that reduces the value of balance sheet assets under its operative accounting framework, gross up the leverage ratio exposure measure by the amount of collateral provided.
fulfilmentPolicy: Capital Management Policy; Collateral Management Policy

section: Domain A-SACCR — SA-CCR Granular Obligations (D7/2020)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D7/2020** §2.4.2 — Cash variation margin treatment. `§2.4.2: below are met, the bank — (a) may regard the cash portion of any variation margin exchanged between counterparties as a form of pre-settlement payment; and (b) may reduce the replacement cost portion of the exposure measure with the cash portion of the variation margin received and the bank may deduct from the exposure measure the receivable asset(s) in respect of the cash variation margin provided: (i) in the case of cash variation margin received, the receiving bank may reduce the replacement cost, but not the PFE, of the exposure amount of the derivative asset by the amount of cash received if the positive mark-to-market value has not already been reduced by the same amount; and (ii) in the case of cash variation margin provided to a counterparty, the posting bank may deduct any resulting receivable from its relevant exposure measure.`
requirement: Apply the prescribed conditions for treating cash variation margin as a pre-settlement payment: reduce replacement cost (not PFE) by cash variation margin received; deduct the receivable for cash variation margin provided; apply the prescribed eligibility conditions for this treatment as set out in D7/2020.
fulfilmentPolicy: Capital Management Policy; Collateral Management Policy; Margin Policy

section: Domain A-SACCR — SA-CCR Granular Obligations (D7/2020)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D7/2020** §2.5.1 — Clearing-member exposure treatment. `§2.5.1: When the bank acts as a clearing member and offers clearing services to clients: (a) where the bank is obliged to reimburse a client for losses if CCP defaults, capture all relevant trade exposures to the CCP similarly to other derivatives, including variation margin in the exposure amount whether or not insolvency-remote; (b) where the bank has no such obligation for QCCP defaults, may exclude relevant trade exposure amounts; (c) where the bank guarantees client derivative exposures to the CCP, calculate related leverage ratio exposure as a derivative exposure as if directly entered with the client.`
requirement: Where the bank acts as a clearing member, apply the prescribed treatment for trade exposures to CCPs and client-clearing guarantees in the leverage ratio exposure measure per D7/2020 §2.5.1.
fulfilmentPolicy: Capital Management Policy; Clearing & Settlement Policy

section: Domain A-SACCR — SA-CCR Granular Obligations (D7/2020)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D7/2020** §2.6.1 — Written credit derivative notional inclusion. `§2.6.1: Since a written credit derivative instrument creates a notional credit exposure that arises from the creditworthiness of the relevant reference entity, a bank shall, in addition to the CCR exposure arising from the fair value of the relevant contract and any related collateral, treat any written credit derivative instrument consistently with cash instruments, such as loans or bonds, for the purposes of the bank's exposure measure.` + §2.6.2: Include in the exposure measure the effective notional amount referenced by the written credit derivative instrument, reducible by negative fair-value changes reflected in Tier 1 capital.
requirement: For written credit derivative instruments, include the effective notional amount in the leverage ratio exposure measure in addition to the CCR exposure from fair value, treating written credit derivatives consistently with cash instruments such as loans or bonds.
fulfilmentPolicy: Capital Management Policy; Market Risk Policy; Credit Risk Policy

section: Domain A-SACCR — SA-CCR Granular Obligations (D7/2020)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D7/2020** §2.6.3 — Purchased credit derivative offset against written credit derivative. `§2.6.3: The bank may reduce the resulting amount by the effective notional amount of a purchased credit derivative instrument on the reference name, provided: (a) same/identical reference name; (b) remaining maturity of protection purchased ≥ remaining maturity of written instrument; (c) effective notional of offsetting purchased credit protection reduced by positive fair-value change in Tier 1; (d) for single-name credit derivatives: protection purchased on pari-passu-or-junior obligation; (e) protection purchased on a pool may offset sold protection on individual names only if economically equivalent to buying separately on each name; (f) partial-pool protection — no offsetting permitted for protection sold on individual reference names.`
requirement: Apply the permitted offsets for purchased credit protection against written credit derivative exposure in the leverage ratio, subject to the reference-entity identity, maturity, seniority, and economic-equivalence conditions set out in D7/2020 §2.6.3.
fulfilmentPolicy: Capital Management Policy; Credit Risk Policy; Hedging Policy

section: Domain A-SACCR — SA-CCR Granular Obligations (D7/2020)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D7/2020** §2.6.4 — Total return swap credit protection not recognised. `§2.6.4: When the bank buys credit protection through a total return swap (TRS) and records the net payments received as net income, but does not record offsetting deterioration in the value of the written credit derivative, either through reductions in fair value or by an addition to reserves, reflected in the bank's tier 1 capital, the credit protection shall not be recognised for the purpose of offsetting the effective notional amounts related to written credit derivative instruments.`
requirement: Where credit protection is purchased via a total return swap but offsetting deterioration in written credit derivative value is not reflected in Tier 1 capital (as fair value reduction or reserves addition), not recognise the TRS protection as an offset against written credit derivative notional in the leverage ratio exposure measure.
fulfilmentPolicy: Capital Management Policy; Market Risk Policy; Hedging Policy

section: Domain A-SACCR — SA-CCR Granular Obligations (D7/2020)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D7/2020** §2.7 — Implementation date. `§2.7: Banks must comply with this directive simultaneously with the implementation of the amended Regulations that incorporate the SA-CCR methodology.` + D7/2020 §3.1 (Acknowledgement of Receipt obligation): `§3.1: Kindly ensure that a copy of this Directive is made available to your institution's external auditors. The attached acknowledgment of receipt duly completed and signed by both the chief executive officer of the institution and the said auditors should be returned to the PA at the earliest convenience.` Issued by: Kuben Naidoo, Deputy Governor and CEO: Prudential Authority, Date: 2020-12-01.
requirement: Comply with Directive D7/2020 (SA-CCR leverage ratio methodology) simultaneously with the implementation of the amended Regulations incorporating SA-CCR; provide the directive to external auditors; return the completed acknowledgement of receipt signed by the CEO and auditors to the PA at the earliest convenience.
fulfilmentPolicy: Regulatory Engagement Policy; Capital Management Policy

citation: **Companies Act 71/2008 s.24–26** — accounting records and registers: s.24 (accounting records must be kept in written form or in a form capable of being converted to written form); s.25 (accounting records must fairly reflect the state of affairs); s.26 (every company must retain accounting records, shareholder registers, directors' service contracts, and annual financial statements for **at least 7 years** from the date of the relevant act) `[citation: Companies Act 71/2008 ss.24–26]`

section: Domain RM — Internal-policy citation handles (records management, operational-substrate retention)
citation: **Companies Act 71/2008 s.28** — accounting records: the company's accounting records must fairly represent the state of affairs and business of the company; accounting records must be kept at the company's registered office or at another location disclosed to the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) `[citation: Companies Act 71/2008 s.28]`
requirement: Maintain accounting records that fairly represent the company's state of affairs and business, keep them at the registered office or disclose any alternate location to the CIPC, and make them available for inspection by any authorised officer, auditor, or regulator on demand.

Cross-reference `ORG-PR(IV)-03` (POPIA s.14 in Domain IV privacy domain) and `ORG-RM-01` (Records Management Policy citation handle noting POPIA s.14 as part of the policy's citation chain).
requirement: Retain personal information only for as long as required to fulfil the purpose of collection or any applicable statutory floor, and destroy or de-identify it promptly and securely once that period expires, per POPIA s.14.

section: Domain RM — Internal-policy citation handles (records management, operational-substrate retention)

Cross-reference `ORG-EL-*` ECTA domain rows for the broader ECTA posture.
requirement: Ensure electronic records satisfy the ECTA ss.15–16 integrity and attribution requirements: accessible for subsequent reference, reproducible in intelligible form at any time, and with determinable origin and creation time; and that electronic signatures meet the ECTA s.13 reliability standard where a signature is legally required.
