section: Domain RM-RDARR — Effective Risk Data Aggregation and Risk Reporting (D2/2015 / BCBS 239)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D2/2015** §1.1–§1.2 + §2.1–§2.2 — Governance and infrastructure overarch (BCBS 239 Principles 1–2). `§1.2: Effective risk data aggregation and risk reporting. §2.2: Institutions are required to ensure compliance with the requirements set out herein.` BCBS 239 Principle 1 (Governance): A bank should establish a strong governance framework for risk data aggregation capabilities and risk reporting practices, covering approval of the data aggregation and reporting framework by the board; senior management accountability; written policies and procedures; and data quality controls. BCBS 239 Principle 2 (Data Architecture and IT Infrastructure): A bank should design, build and maintain data architecture and IT infrastructure which fully supports its risk data aggregation capabilities and risk reporting practices not only in normal times but also in times of stress or crisis. Enabling authority: Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a); Reg 39 (corporate governance and risk management).
requirement: Establish a strong governance framework for risk data aggregation and risk reporting as required by BCBS 239 Principle 1, including board approval of the RDARR framework, senior management accountability, written policies and procedures, and data quality controls; and design, build, and maintain data architecture and IT infrastructure that fully supports risk data aggregation and risk reporting in both normal and stressed conditions (BCBS 239 Principle 2).
fulfilmentPolicy: Risk Data Aggregation and Reporting Policy; Data Governance Policy; Operational Risk Policy

section: Domain RM-RDARR — Effective Risk Data Aggregation and Risk Reporting (D2/2015 / BCBS 239)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D2/2015** §1.2 + §2.2 — Risk data accuracy and integrity (BCBS 239 Principle 3). BCBS 239 Principle 3 (Accuracy and Integrity): A bank should be able to generate accurate and reliable risk data to meet normal and stress/crisis reporting accuracy requirements. Data should be aggregated on a largely automated basis so as to minimise the probability of errors. A single authoritative source of risk data should exist for each type of risk.
requirement: Aggregate risk data so as to be able to generate accurate and reliable risk data to meet normal and stress/crisis reporting accuracy requirements; base aggregation largely on automated processes to minimise error probability; maintain a single authoritative source of risk data for each risk type.
fulfilmentPolicy: Data Management Policy §6.1; Data Quality Policy

section: Domain RM-RDARR — Effective Risk Data Aggregation and Risk Reporting (D2/2015 / BCBS 239)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D2/2015** §1.2 + §2.2 — Risk data completeness and timeliness (BCBS 239 Principles 4–5). BCBS 239 Principle 4 (Completeness): A bank should be able to capture and aggregate all material risk data across the banking group; data should be available by business line, legal entity, asset type, industry, region, and other groupings as relevant for the risk in question; this allows identification and reporting of risk exposures, concentrations and emerging risks. BCBS 239 Principle 5 (Timeliness): A bank should be able to generate aggregate and up-to-date risk data in a timely manner while also meeting the principles relating to accuracy and integrity; the precise timing will depend on the nature and potential volatility of the risk being measured as well as its criticality to the overall risk profile of the bank.
requirement: Capture and aggregate all material risk data across the banking group with completeness across business lines, legal entities, asset types, industries, and regions to enable risk exposure and concentration identification (BCBS 239 Principle 4); generate aggregate and up-to-date risk data in a timely manner, with timeliness requirements calibrated to the nature and volatility of each risk type (BCBS 239 Principle 5).
fulfilmentPolicy: Risk Data Aggregation and Reporting Policy; Data Governance Policy; Risk Management Framework

section: Domain RM-RDARR — Effective Risk Data Aggregation and Risk Reporting (D2/2015 / BCBS 239)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D2/2015** §1.2 + §2.2 — Risk data adaptability (BCBS 239 Principle 6). BCBS 239 Principle 6 (Adaptability): A bank should be able to generate aggregate risk data to meet a broad range of on-demand, ad hoc risk reporting requests, including requests during stress/crisis situations; a bank should be able to generate aggregate risk data for new risk types or for new business areas and produce sub-consolidated or individual entity risk data.
requirement: Generate aggregate risk data on demand and in ad hoc scenarios — including during stress or crisis situations — covering new risk types, new business areas, and sub-consolidated or individual entity-level data (BCBS 239 Principle 6).
fulfilmentPolicy: Risk Data Aggregation and Reporting Policy; Stress Testing Policy

section: Domain RM-RDARR — Effective Risk Data Aggregation and Risk Reporting (D2/2015 / BCBS 239)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D2/2015** §1.2 + §2.2 — Risk reporting accuracy and clarity (BCBS 239 Principle 7). BCBS 239 Principle 7 (Accuracy): Risk management reports should accurately and precisely convey aggregated risk data and reflect risk in an exact manner; reports should be reconciled and validated; significant data gaps should be identified and explained; any manual intervention in the reporting process should be clearly documented.
requirement: Produce risk management reports that accurately and precisely convey aggregated risk data, are reconciled and validated, identify and explain any significant data gaps, and document any manual interventions in the reporting process (BCBS 239 Principle 7).
fulfilmentPolicy: Risk Data Aggregation and Reporting Policy; Regulatory Reporting Policy

section: Domain RM-RDARR — Effective Risk Data Aggregation and Risk Reporting (D2/2015 / BCBS 239)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D2/2015** §1.2 + §2.2 — Risk reporting comprehensiveness and clarity (BCBS 239 Principles 8–9). BCBS 239 Principle 8 (Comprehensiveness): Risk management reports should cover all material risk areas within the organisation; the depth and scope of these reports should be consistent with the size and complexity of the bank's operations and risk profile, and the requirements of the recipients; forward-looking assessments of risk should be provided. BCBS 239 Principle 9 (Clarity and Usefulness): Risk management reports should communicate information in a clear and concise manner; reports should be easy to understand yet comprehensive enough to allow recipients to make informed decisions; reports should include information on both absolute and relative levels of risk.
requirement: Produce risk management reports that cover all material risk areas with depth and scope calibrated to the bank's size, complexity, and recipients' requirements, including forward-looking assessments (BCBS 239 Principle 8); and present information clearly and concisely to enable informed decisions, covering both absolute and relative risk levels (BCBS 239 Principle 9).
fulfilmentPolicy: Risk Data Aggregation and Reporting Policy; Risk Management Framework

section: Domain RM-RDARR — Effective Risk Data Aggregation and Risk Reporting (D2/2015 / BCBS 239)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D2/2015** §1.2 + §2.2 — Risk reporting frequency and distribution (BCBS 239 Principles 10–11). BCBS 239 Principle 10 (Frequency): The board and senior management should set the frequency of risk management report production and distribution; the frequency of reports should be increased during times of stress/crisis; reports for the board and senior management should be produced at least monthly. BCBS 239 Principle 11 (Distribution): Risk management reports should be distributed to the relevant parties while ensuring that the information remains confidential.
requirement: Set the frequency of risk management report production and distribution, with at least monthly reporting to the board and senior management; increase reporting frequency during stress or crisis conditions (BCBS 239 Principle 10); distribute risk reports to relevant recipients while maintaining confidentiality of the information (BCBS 239 Principle 11).
fulfilmentPolicy: Risk Data Aggregation and Reporting Policy; Information Security Policy

section: Domain RM-RDARR — Effective Risk Data Aggregation and Risk Reporting (D2/2015 / BCBS 239)
citation: SARB Prudential Authority **Directive D2/2015** §2.1 (Application scope) + §2.2 (compliance obligation) — Supervisory review and remediation (BCBS 239 Principles 12–14). BCBS 239 Principle 12 (Review): Supervisors should periodically review and evaluate a bank's compliance with the eleven principles above; supervisors should make use of multiple evaluative techniques — using a range of supervisory tools — to conduct such evaluations. BCBS 239 Principle 13 (Remedial Actions and Supervisory Measures): Supervisors should have and use the appropriate tools and resources to require effective and timely remedial action by a bank to address deficiencies in its risk data aggregation capabilities and risk reporting practices; supervisors should provide appropriate capacity to execute such oversight. BCBS 239 Principle 14 (Home/Host Cooperation): Home and host supervisors of internationally active banks should cooperate with each other and regularly share relevant supervisory information on the risk data aggregation and risk reporting practices of the banks they oversee, in line with the information-sharing principles in the Basel Committee's Core Principles for Effective Banking Supervision. `§2.1: This directive applies to all banks, branches of foreign institutions and controlling companies registered or operating in South Africa. §2.2: Institutions are required to ensure compliance with the requirements set out herein.`
requirement: Comply with all BCBS 239 principles (1–11) as required by D2/2015, including readiness for supervisory review under Principles 12–14: maintain documented risk data aggregation and reporting frameworks sufficient to support PA supervisory evaluation; remediate any deficiencies identified by supervisory review in a timely manner; and ensure cross-border cooperation readiness under the home/host cooperation principle where applicable.
fulfilmentPolicy: Data Management Policy §6.1; Regulatory Engagement Policy; `Procedures/by-policy/ba-returns-regulation-46.md` (planned)

section: Domain H — Tax

section: Domain H — Tax

section: Domain H — Tax

section: Domain G — Corporate governance / board
citation: SARB PA Directive D1/2026 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Matters related to the promotion of sound corporate governance in relation to the appointment of directors and executive officers
requirement: Banks must ensure that all directors and executive officers meet fit-and-proper requirements prior to appointment, submit completed form BA 020 to the PA, and comply with the PA's prescribed corporate governance framework for appointments.
fulfilmentPolicy: Corporate Governance Policy

section: Domain G — Corporate governance / board
citation: SARB PA Directive D2/2008 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Procedure to be followed in respect of applications in terms of sections 37, 52 and/or 54 of the Banks Act
requirement: Banks must follow the PA's prescribed procedure and submit all required information when making applications under sections 37 (acquisitions/amalgamations), 52 (shareholding changes) and/or 54 of the Banks Act.
fulfilmentPolicy: Regulatory Applications Policy

section: Domain B — Market risk
citation: SARB PA Directive D2/2011 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Reporting daily value-at-risk amounts for market risk using specified items of the form BA 325
requirement: Banks using internal models for market risk must report daily VaR amounts to the PA using the specified items of BA 325 form, with all VaR figures calculated using PA-prescribed methodology and confidence intervals.
fulfilmentPolicy: Market Risk Policy

section: Domain D — Credit risk / counterparty
citation: SARB PA Directive D2/2014 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Matters related to changes to internal rating systems used to calculate minimum required capital for credit risk
requirement: Banks using the IRB approach must obtain prior PA approval before making material changes to their internal rating systems, and must notify the PA of non-material changes within prescribed timelines.
fulfilmentPolicy: Credit Risk Policy

section: Domain H — Accounting & reporting
citation: SARB PA Directive D2/2015 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Effective risk data aggregation and risk reporting (BCBS 239)
requirement: Banks must implement and maintain risk data aggregation and risk reporting capabilities that comply with BCBS 239 principles, including data accuracy, integrity, completeness, timeliness and adaptability.
fulfilmentPolicy: Risk Data Aggregation Policy

section: Domain H — Accounting & reporting
citation: SARB PA Directive D2/2017 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Matters relating to the communication of key audit matters in the independent auditor's report
requirement: Banks must ensure their appointed auditors communicate key audit matters in the independent auditor's report in accordance with the PA's prescribed requirements and in addition to applicable auditing standards.
fulfilmentPolicy: External Audit Policy

section: Domain A — Prudential (capital, liquidity, large exposures, leverage)
citation: SARB PA Directive D2/2018 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Materiality threshold in respect of exposure to a foreign jurisdiction in applying jurisdictional reciprocity in the countercyclical capital buffer calculation
requirement: Banks must apply the PA-prescribed materiality threshold when determining whether to recognise a foreign jurisdiction's countercyclical buffer rate under jurisdictional reciprocity, and must document and report this determination.
fulfilmentPolicy: Capital Management Policy

section: Domain C — Operational risk
citation: SARB PA Directive D2/2019 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Reporting of material information technology and/or cyber incidents
requirement: Banks must report material IT and/or cyber incidents to the PA within the prescribed timeframes using the prescribed reporting template, and must maintain an internal incident log with all required data fields.
fulfilmentPolicy: Operational Risk Policy

section: Domain A — Prudential (capital, liquidity, large exposures, leverage)
citation: SARB PA Directive D2/2021 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Matters related to the issuance of additional tier 1 capital instruments that contain contingent must-pay clauses
requirement: Banks including contingent must-pay clauses in AT1 capital instruments must not obtain PA approval for instruments that would exclude such clauses from triggering loss absorbency, and must notify the PA of any proposed AT1 instrument that includes such a clause before issuance.
fulfilmentPolicy: Capital Instruments Policy

section: Domain G — Corporate governance / board
citation: SARB PA Directive D2/2022 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Requirements for conducting the business of a representative office of a foreign banking institution in South Africa
requirement: A representative office of a foreign banking institution operating in South Africa must comply with the PA's prescribed requirements regarding permissible activities, registration, reporting and conduct, and must not conduct deposit-taking or credit business.
fulfilmentPolicy: Corporate Governance Policy

section: Domain H — Accounting & reporting
citation: SARB PA Directive D2/2023 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Directive for the completion of the form BA 330 (IRRBB)
requirement: Banks must complete form BA 330 (interest rate risk in the banking book) in accordance with the PA's prescribed instructions and submit it within prescribed timelines.
fulfilmentPolicy: Regulatory Reporting Policy

section: Domain H — Accounting & reporting
citation: SARB PA Directive D2/2024 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Reporting requirements in terms of regulation 46 of the Regulations relating to Banks
requirement: Banks must comply with the reporting requirements under regulation 46 of the RRB, including submission of prescribed returns within specified timeframes and in the prescribed format.
fulfilmentPolicy: Regulatory Reporting Policy

section: Domain A — Prudential (capital, liquidity, large exposures, leverage)
citation: SARB PA Directive D2/2025 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Matters related to the capital treatment of significant investments in insurance entities
requirement: Banks holding significant investments in insurance entities must apply the PA-prescribed capital treatment (deduction from CET1 or risk-weighted at 250%) and must not double-count such investments in the group's capital base.
fulfilmentPolicy: Capital Management Policy

section: Domain G — Corporate governance / board
citation: SARB PA Directive D3/2008 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Appointment of directors or executive officers, and completion of form BA 020
requirement: Banks must complete and submit form BA 020 to the PA for every appointment or change of a director or executive officer, prior to or within the prescribed period after the appointment.
fulfilmentPolicy: Corporate Governance Policy

section: Domain A — Prudential (capital, liquidity, large exposures, leverage)
citation: SARB PA Directive D3/2017 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Assets lodged or pledged to secure liabilities
requirement: Banks must report to the PA all assets lodged or pledged to secure liabilities in excess of prescribed thresholds, using the prescribed reporting format and within the prescribed timeframes.
fulfilmentPolicy: Liquidity Risk Policy

section: Domain C — Operational risk
citation: SARB PA Directive D3/2018 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Cloud computing and the offshoring of data
requirement: Banks using cloud computing services or offshoring data must notify or obtain approval from the PA where required, conduct prescribed risk assessments, maintain data sovereignty and audit rights, and ensure the PA can access data on request.
fulfilmentPolicy: Operational Risk Policy

section: Domain H — Accounting & reporting
citation: SARB PA Directive D3/2023 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Regulatory treatment of accounting provisions
requirement: Banks must apply the PA-prescribed regulatory treatment of IFRS 9 and other accounting provisions when calculating regulatory capital, including the transition arrangements and the treatment of stage 1, 2 and 3 provisions.
fulfilmentPolicy: Capital Management Policy

section: Domain A — Prudential (capital, liquidity, large exposures, leverage)
citation: SARB PA Directive D3/2024 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Minimum regulatory requirements relating to deposits covered by the Corporation for Deposit Insurance and banks' fund liquidity contributions
requirement: Banks must comply with PA requirements for identifying CODI-covered deposits, making fund liquidity contributions, and meeting prescribed minimum requirements for the deposit insurance scheme.
fulfilmentPolicy: Liquidity Risk Policy

section: Domain A — Prudential (capital, liquidity, large exposures, leverage)
citation: SARB PA Directive D3/2025 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Matters related to the leverage ratio buffer requirement for domestic systemically important banks
requirement: D-SIBs must maintain the PA-prescribed leverage ratio buffer (concomitant tier 1 leverage requirement) above the minimum leverage ratio, with capital distribution constraints applying when the buffer is breached.
fulfilmentPolicy: Capital Management Policy

section: Domain H — Accounting & reporting
citation: SARB PA Directive D4/2008 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Disclosure of repurchase and resale agreements and similar transactions
requirement: Banks must disclose repurchase agreements, reverse repurchase agreements and similar transactions in their financial statements in accordance with the PA's prescribed format and classification requirements.
fulfilmentPolicy: Regulatory Reporting Policy

section: Domain A — Prudential (capital, liquidity, large exposures, leverage)
citation: SARB PA Directive D4/2015 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Amendments to the Regulations relating to Banks, and matters related thereto
requirement: Banks must implement the amendments to the Regulations Relating to Banks prescribed by D4/2015 and ensure all affected processes, models, returns and policies are updated accordingly.
fulfilmentPolicy: Capital Management Policy

section: Domain A — Prudential (capital, liquidity, large exposures, leverage)
citation: SARB PA Directive D4/2017 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Matters related to securitisation vehicles
requirement: Banks sponsoring or using securitisation vehicles must comply with the PA's prescribed criteria for recognition of risk transfer, treatment of securitisation exposures, and capital requirements for retained interests.
fulfilmentPolicy: Credit Risk Policy

section: Domain A — Prudential (capital, liquidity, large exposures, leverage)
citation: SARB PA Directive D4/2021 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Externally facilitated liquidity stress simulations
requirement: Banks must participate in PA-facilitated liquidity stress simulations when required, provide all requested data and information, and implement remediation actions arising from simulation findings within PA-prescribed timeframes.
fulfilmentPolicy: Liquidity Risk Policy

section: Domain F — Financial crime / AML
citation: SARB PA Directive D4/2022 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Requirement to submit anti-money laundering and counter-financing of terrorism risk returns to the PA on a periodic basis
requirement: Banks must submit AML/CFT risk returns to the PA on a periodic basis as prescribed, using the prescribed template and including all required risk assessment data and metrics.
fulfilmentPolicy: AML/CFT Policy

section: Domain C — Operational risk
citation: SARB PA Directive D4/2023 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Directive on operational resilience
requirement: Banks must establish and maintain an operational resilience framework covering identification of critical business services, impact tolerances, scenario testing, and remediation plans, in accordance with PA-prescribed standards.
fulfilmentPolicy: Operational Risk Policy

section: Domain H — Accounting & reporting
citation: SARB PA Directive D4/2025 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Completion of regulatory return: form BA 701
requirement: Banks must complete and submit form BA 701 (recovery planning and resolution) in accordance with the PA's prescribed instructions and within prescribed submission deadlines.
fulfilmentPolicy: Regulatory Reporting Policy

section: Domain H — Accounting & reporting
citation: SARB PA Directive D5/2011 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Exemption from certain minimum disclosure requirements pertaining to branches of foreign institutions
requirement: Branches of foreign institutions may apply to the PA for exemption from certain Pillar 3 disclosure requirements where the home country makes equivalent disclosures, and must meet PA conditions for maintaining such exemption.
fulfilmentPolicy: Pillar 3 Disclosure Policy

section: Domain H — Accounting & reporting
citation: SARB PA Directive D5/2016 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Compliance with principles for effective risk data aggregation and risk reporting
requirement: Systemically important banks must demonstrate compliance with BCBS 239 risk data aggregation and risk reporting principles and submit self-assessments to the PA on a prescribed basis.
fulfilmentPolicy: Risk Data Aggregation Policy

section: Domain B — Market risk
citation: SARB PA Directive D5/2020 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Prudent Valuation Adjustments Framework
requirement: Banks must apply the PA-prescribed Prudent Valuation Adjustments (PVA) framework to all fair-valued positions, calculate Additional Valuation Adjustments (AVAs), and deduct resulting PVAs from CET1 capital.
fulfilmentPolicy: Market Risk Policy

section: Domain A — Prudential (capital, liquidity, large exposures, leverage)
citation: SARB PA Directive D5/2021 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Capital framework for South Africa based on the Basel III framework
requirement: Banks must comply with the SA implementation of the Basel III capital framework as prescribed by the PA, including minimum CET1, Tier 1 and Total Capital ratios, conservation buffers, countercyclical buffers and D-SIB surcharges.
fulfilmentPolicy: Capital Management Policy

section: Domain A — Prudential (capital, liquidity, large exposures, leverage)
citation: SARB PA Directive D5/2022 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Matters relating to liquidity risk
requirement: Banks must maintain liquidity risk management frameworks compliant with PA prescribed standards, including HQLA composition requirements, intraday liquidity monitoring, and adherence to LCR and NSFR minimum thresholds.
fulfilmentPolicy: Liquidity Risk Policy

section: Domain A — Prudential (capital, liquidity, large exposures, leverage)
citation: SARB PA Directive D5/2024 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Loss absorbency requirements for additional tier 1 and tier 2 capital instruments
requirement: AT1 and T2 capital instruments issued by banks must include contractual loss-absorbency triggers and write-down/conversion mechanisms as prescribed by the PA, and must comply with updated Basel III eligibility criteria.
fulfilmentPolicy: Capital Instruments Policy

section: Domain H — Accounting & reporting
citation: SARB PA Directive D5/2025 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Returns to be submitted to the Prudential Authority
requirement: Banks must submit all regulatory returns to the PA in the prescribed format, frequency, and within prescribed deadlines as listed in the returns schedule accompanying D5/2025.
fulfilmentPolicy: Regulatory Reporting Policy

section: Domain H — Accounting & reporting
citation: SARB PA Directive D6/2008 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Auditor rotation
requirement: Banks must rotate their audit engagement partner and designated auditor within PA-prescribed maximum tenure periods and must not appoint a recently rotated auditor for a prescribed cooling-off period.
fulfilmentPolicy: External Audit Policy

section: Domain A — Prudential (capital, liquidity, large exposures, leverage)
citation: SARB PA Directive D6/2017 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Process in terms of specific capital issuances and redemptions
requirement: Banks must follow the PA-prescribed process for obtaining approval prior to issuing or redeeming qualifying capital instruments, including submission of prescribed documentation and timelines.
fulfilmentPolicy: Capital Instruments Policy

section: Domain D — Credit risk / counterparty
citation: SARB PA Directive D6/2021 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Matters related to the use of credit risk models to calculate minimum required capital for specialised lending exposures relating to project finance portfolios
requirement: Banks using credit risk models for project finance specialised lending exposures must obtain PA approval for those models, comply with PA-prescribed model criteria, and report model outputs as prescribed.
fulfilmentPolicy: Credit Risk Policy

section: Domain G — Corporate governance / board
citation: SARB PA Directive D6/2022 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Matters related to fit-and-proper assessment requirements pertaining to beneficial owners
requirement: Banks must conduct PA-prescribed fit-and-proper assessments of beneficial owners who hold qualifying shareholdings, and must submit results to the PA in the prescribed format and within prescribed timelines.
fulfilmentPolicy: Corporate Governance Policy

section: Domain A — Prudential (capital, liquidity, large exposures, leverage)
citation: SARB PA Directive D6/2024 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Implementation of a positive cycle-neutral countercyclical capital buffer
requirement: Banks must maintain a positive cycle-neutral countercyclical capital buffer (CCyB) rate as prescribed by the PA, and incorporate this buffer into their regulatory capital calculations from the effective date.
fulfilmentPolicy: Capital Management Policy

section: Domain H — Accounting & reporting
citation: SARB PA Directive D6/2025 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Returns to be submitted to the PA with effect from 1 July 2025
requirement: Banks must submit all regulatory returns in accordance with the updated schedule effective 1 July 2025 as prescribed in D6/2025, including any new or amended forms introduced by Basel III post-crisis reforms.
fulfilmentPolicy: Regulatory Reporting Policy

section: Domain D — Credit risk / counterparty
citation: SARB PA Directive D7/2015 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Restructured credit exposures
requirement: Banks must classify, measure and report restructured credit exposures in accordance with the PA's prescribed definitions and criteria, and must not cease to classify an exposure as restructured until all PA exit criteria are met.
fulfilmentPolicy: Credit Risk Policy

section: Domain A — Prudential (capital, liquidity, large exposures, leverage)
citation: SARB PA Directive D7/2016 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Assessment of instruments issued by domestic systemically important banks and controlling companies for capital and funding purposes
requirement: D-SIBs must have all qualifying capital and funding instruments assessed by the PA prior to issuance, and must submit the full terms and conditions of proposed instruments with the assessment request.
fulfilmentPolicy: Capital Instruments Policy

section: Domain A — Prudential (capital, liquidity, large exposures, leverage)
citation: SARB PA Directive D7/2020 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Calculation of derivative exposure amount for the purposes of determining the leverage ratio
requirement: Banks must calculate derivative exposure amounts for leverage ratio purposes using the SA-CCR method as prescribed by the PA, replacing the Current Exposure Method from the prescribed effective date.
fulfilmentPolicy: Capital Management Policy

section: Domain G — Corporate governance / board
citation: SARB PA Directive D7/2022 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Matters related to fit-and-proper assessment requirements pertaining to directors and executive officers
requirement: Banks must conduct and document PA-prescribed fit-and-proper assessments of all directors and executive officers at appointment and on an ongoing basis, and must submit assessment results to the PA within prescribed timelines.
fulfilmentPolicy: Corporate Governance Policy

section: Domain D — Credit risk / counterparty
citation: SARB PA Directive D7/2023 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Directive on matters relating to eligible external credit assessment institutions
requirement: Banks using the standardised approach for credit risk must only use credit ratings from PA-designated eligible external credit assessment institutions (ECAIs) and must map ECAI ratings to risk weights in accordance with PA prescribed tables.
fulfilmentPolicy: Credit Risk Policy

section: Domain H — Accounting & reporting
citation: SARB PA Directive D7/2025 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — South African domestic systemically important banks to submit consolidated information
requirement: South African D-SIBs must submit consolidated financial, risk and regulatory information to the PA in the prescribed format, frequency and scope, covering the full banking group.
fulfilmentPolicy: Regulatory Reporting Policy

section: Domain A — Prudential (capital, liquidity, large exposures, leverage)
citation: SARB PA Directive D8/2014 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Matters related to compliance with the liquidity coverage ratio
requirement: Banks must maintain an LCR of at least 100% at all times as prescribed and must notify the PA immediately if the LCR falls or is expected to fall below the minimum, with a remediation plan submitted within prescribed timelines.
fulfilmentPolicy: Liquidity Risk Policy

section: Domain C — Operational risk
citation: SARB PA Directive D8/2016 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Reporting requirements relating to material outsourced service providers and critical third-party service providers
requirement: Banks must report material outsourced service providers and critical third-party service providers to the PA on a prescribed basis, and must notify the PA of any material changes to such arrangements within prescribed timeframes.
fulfilmentPolicy: Operational Risk Policy

section: Domain D — Credit risk / counterparty
citation: SARB PA Directive D8/2025 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Threshold amounts for the revised standardised and IRB approaches for credit risk, liquidity risk and IRRBB frameworks
requirement: Banks must apply the PA-prescribed threshold amounts when implementing the revised standardised approach (SA-CR), IRB approaches for credit risk, liquidity risk frameworks, and IRRBB requirements, effective from prescribed implementation dates.
fulfilmentPolicy: Credit Risk Policy

section: Domain Q — Group structure / entities
citation: SARB PA Directive D9/2013 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Investments, and loans and advances by controlling companies: section 50 of the Banks Act
requirement: Controlling companies of banks must comply with the PA's prescribed restrictions on investments, loans and advances to connected parties under section 50 of the Banks Act, and must obtain PA approval for transactions exceeding prescribed thresholds.
fulfilmentPolicy: Corporate Governance Policy

section: Domain C — Operational risk
citation: SARB PA Directive D9/2021 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Principles for the sound management of operational risk
requirement: Banks must implement a comprehensive operational risk management framework aligned with the PA's prescribed principles, covering governance, risk identification and assessment, control environment, monitoring, and reporting.
fulfilmentPolicy: Operational Risk Policy

section: Domain F — Financial crime / AML
citation: SARB PA Directive D9/2022 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Matters relating to domestic money or value transfer services
requirement: Banks providing or facilitating domestic money or value transfer services must comply with PA-prescribed prudential and conduct requirements, including AML/CFT obligations, reporting and customer identification.
fulfilmentPolicy: AML/CFT Policy

section: Domain D — Credit risk / counterparty
citation: SARB PA Directive D9/2025 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Prudential treatment of credit exposures secured by forest and agricultural land
requirement: Banks must apply the PA-prescribed risk weights and eligibility criteria when determining the prudential treatment of credit exposures secured by forest or agricultural land as collateral.
fulfilmentPolicy: Credit Risk Policy

section: Domain B — Market risk
citation: SARB PA Directive D10/2013 (Banks Act 94/1990 s.6(6)(a)) — Limit in respect of effective net open foreign currency position, and matters related to unencumbered assets for branches of foreign institutions
requirement: Banks must not allow their effective net open foreign currency position to exceed the PA-prescribed limit relative to qualifying capital, and branches of foreign institutions must maintain prescribed levels of unencumbered assets in South Africa.
fulfilmentPolicy: Market Risk Policy
